mainTopic: רב ששת's escape from the servants, and how שלמה captured אשמדאי to find the שמיר
overview: This amud finishes the story of רב ששת at the house of ריש גלותא. The hostile servants find his uneaten meat hidden in his scarf. רב ששת proves, using a rule of רב חסדא, that the meat came from a sick animal. The servants then hide a pit to trap him, but a warning snort from רב חסדא, a child's פסוק and his own suspicion help him avoid it. Next the גמרא explains a פסוק in קהלת about שלמה's luxuries, which in בבל was read as saying שלמה had demons. To build the בית המקדש without iron, שלמה needed the שמיר, and the demons sent him to אשמדאי, their king. בניהו tricks אשמדאי with wine, chains him with God's Name, and starts bringing him back. The story continues on the next amud at a widow's hut.

steps.title: The servants stage a theft and find the hidden meat
steps.stepSummary: The servants claim a silver cup was stolen so they can search everyone, and they find the meat wrapped in רב ששת's scarf.
steps.simpleTranslation: "A silver cup was stolen from us!" While they were searching and coming around, they found the meat wrapped in his scarf.
steps.whatsHappening: The servants announce a fake theft as an excuse to search everyone. During the search they find רב ששת's piece of meat hidden in his scarf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story is setting up a conflict. רב ששת did not eat the meat he was served, and now the servants have "caught" him hiding it. This leads straight into their complaint in the next step.

phrases.english: A silver cup was stolen from us!
While they were checking and coming around,
they found it wrapped in his scarf.
phrases.notes: "It" is the piece of meat רב ששת was served, and "his" means רב ששת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of רב ששת at ריש גלותא's house from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The servants find the uneaten meat hidden in רב ששת's scarf.

steps.title: The servants accuse רב ששת of insulting them
steps.stepSummary: The servants tell ריש גלותא that רב ששת does not really want to eat; he only wants to upset them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: "See, Master, he doesn't want to eat. He just wants to cause us pain!"
steps.whatsHappening: The servants turn to ריש גלותא and use the hidden meat as evidence against רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their claim is that hiding the meat shows bad intent. In their eyes he is not avoiding the food for a real reason, only to insult the hosts. This is a challenge that רב ששת must now answer.

keyTerms.meaning: to cause us pain / to upset us

phrases.english: They said to him: See, Master,
phrases.notes: The servants are talking to ריש גלותא here.

phrases.english: that he does not want to eat,
but rather to cause us pain!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the discovery from step 1 as an accusation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's behavior in not eating and hiding the meat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Hiding food you were served looks like a deliberate insult to the host.

steps.title: רב ששת explains that the meat tasted of a sick animal
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says he did taste the meat, and it had the taste of white spots, a sign of illness.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: "I did eat, and I tasted in it the taste of white spots."
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the accusation. He says he did taste the meat, but it tasted like it came from a sick animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His answer flips the charge around. He was not insulting anyone; he had a real reason not to eat. The meat seemed to come from an animal with white spots on its skin.

keyTerms.meaning: white (here: white spots, a sign of disease)

phrases.english: He said to them: I did eat,
and I tasted in it a taste of white.
phrases.notes: "White" means white spots on the animal's skin, a sign the animal was sick.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the accusation in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a legitimate reason for the behavior
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He refused the food just to upset the hosts.
steps.terutzMaskana: He refused because the meat tasted like it came from a diseased animal.

steps.title: The servants deny serving a white-spotted animal
steps.stepSummary: The servants say they did not prepare any animal with white spots that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: "We did not prepare any white animal today."
steps.whatsHappening: The servants reject רב ששת's explanation by denying that any such animal was served.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They are attacking the facts of his answer. If no white-spotted animal was prepared, then his excuse seems made up.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: חִיוָּרָא לָא עֲבִיד לַן הָאִידָּנָא.
phrases.english: They said to him: We did not prepare a white one today.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ: חִיוָּרָא לָא עֲבִיד לַן הָאִידָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב ששת's explanation from step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The factual basis of רב ששת's claim
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: They claim no white-spotted animal was served that day.

steps.title: רב ששת tells them to check the skin, based on רב חסדא's rule
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת tells them to check the skin where his portion came from, relying on רב חסדא's rule that mixed black and white spots are a sign of disease.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: "Check at the spot it came from." As רב חסדא said: black spots on white skin, and white spots on black skin, are a sign of disease.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת explains that the animal does not have to be fully white. A white spot on a dark animal is enough, so he tells them to check the exact place his piece came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The servants assumed "white" meant an all-white animal. רב חסדא's rule shows that a patch of a different color, black on white or white on black, is itself a sign of illness. So the test is at the specific place on the skin.

phrases.english: He said to them: Check in its place;
phrases.notes: He means check the animal's skin right where his piece of meat was cut from.

phrases.english: for Rav Chisda said:
Black within white, and white within black,
is an affliction.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: בְּדַקוּ בְּדוּכְתֵּיהּ; דְּאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the denial in step 4 by showing that a spot, not a fully white animal, is the issue.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's claim that the meat came from a diseased animal
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב חסדא's rule that black-on-white or white-on-black spots are a sign of disease
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a color patch alone signals illness. That is why the servants' denial did not settle the matter.

steps.title: They check and find the spot
steps.stepSummary: The servants check the skin and find the diseased spot, proving רב ששת right.
steps.simpleTranslation: They checked and found it.
steps.whatsHappening: The check confirms that רב ששת was right about the sick animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ends the first scene. רב ששת is proven right, but the servants become even angrier, which leads into the next scene.
steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת did not refuse the food to insult anyone. He sensed by taste that the animal was sick, and the check proved it.

phrases.english: They checked and found it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the claim made in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב ששת was right: the animal had a diseased spot.

steps.title: The servants set a hidden pit as a trap
steps.stepSummary: As רב ששת leaves, the servants dig a pit, cover it with a mat, and invite him to sit and rest there.
steps.simpleTranslation: As he was leaving, they dug a pit for him, put a reed mat over it, and said to him: "Let the Master come and rest."
steps.whatsHappening: A new scene begins. The angry servants try to make רב ששת fall into a hidden pit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mat hides the pit so it looks like a place to sit. Their invitation to "rest" is really a trap meant to hurt him.

phrases.english: When he was leaving,
they dug a pit for him
and threw a reed mat over it,
and said to him: Let the Master come and rest.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָא נָפֵיק, כְּרוֹ לֵיהּ בֵּירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second scene after the servants were embarrassed in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The servants set a covered pit to trap רב ששת.

steps.title: Warning signs lead רב ששת to avoid the pit
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא snorts a warning, a child recites a פסוק about turning aside, the attendant sees the mat, and רב ששת goes around it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא snorted at him from behind. רב ששת said to a child: "Tell me your verse." The child said: "Turn to your right or to your left." He said to his attendant: "What do you see?" He answered: "A mat lying there." He said: "Go around it."
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת picks up a warning from רב חסדא and a hint from a child's פסוק. He checks with his attendant and avoids the mat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking a child for the פסוק he learned was a way of looking for a sign. The פסוק "turn to your right or to your left" fits the moment, so רב ששת asks what is in front of him and steers around the mat.

keyTerms.meaning: turn away from it / go around it

phrases.english: Rav Chisda snorted at him from behind.
He said to a child:
Recite your verse for me,
He said to him: "Turn to your right
or to your left."

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיה לְשַׁמָּעֵיהּ: מַאי קָא חָזֵית?
phrases.english: He said to his attendant: What do you see?
He said to him: A mat that is laid down.
He said to him: Go around it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the trap from step 7 fails.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ששת avoids the hidden pit.

steps.title: רב חסדא asks how רב ששת knew
steps.stepSummary: After they leave, רב חסדא asks רב ששת how he knew about the trap.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he left, רב חסדא said to him: "How did the Master know?"
steps.whatsHappening: The scene is over, and רב חסדא asks רב ששת how he figured out the danger. This sets up רב ששת's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא only gave a vague snort. He wants to know what else led רב ששת to suspect a trap.

phrases.english: After he left,
Rav Chisda said to him:
How did the Master know?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְבָתַר דִּנְפַק, אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא: מְנָא הֲוָה יָדַע מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What clues told רב ששת there was a trap?

steps.title: רב ששת lists three clues
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת names three clues: רב חסדא's snort, the child's פסוק, and the fact that servants are not trustworthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: "First, the Master snorted at me. Also, the child recited that verse for me. And also, servants are suspected of not acting honestly."
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת explains that three clues together made him suspicious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No single clue proved anything, but together they pointed to danger. There was a warning from a friend, a hint from the child's פסוק, and the knowledge that these servants were likely to try to harm him.

keyTerms.meaning: behaving honestly / to a high standard

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת avoided the trap by putting three clues together: רב חסדא's warning snort, the child's פסוק about turning aside, and his suspicion of the servants.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲדָא – דִּנְחַר לִי מָר.
phrases.english: He said to him: One, that the Master snorted at me.
And also, that the child recited a verse for me.
And also, that servants are suspected of not being upright.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲדָא – דִּנְחַר לִי מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חסדא's question from step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three clues: רב חסדא's snort, the child's פסוק, and the known untrustworthiness of servants.

steps.title: A verse in קהלת about שלמה's luxuries
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes קהלת 2:8 and explains its first two items: musical instruments, and pools and bathhouses.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I got myself שרים ושרות, and human pleasures, שדה ושדות.' 'שרים ושרות' are kinds of music. 'Human pleasures' are pools and bathhouses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a פסוק in which שלמה lists the luxuries he had, and explains its words one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase of the פסוק gets a short meaning. 'שרים ושרות' means types of music, and 'תענוגות בני האדם' means pools and bathhouses. This prepares for the last phrase, 'שדה ושדות', which is the real focus of the coming section.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'singers, male and female'; explained here as kinds of music
Kinds of music or musical instruments

phrases.english: "I got myself sharim and sharot,
and human pleasures, shidda and shiddot";
"Sharim and sharot": these are kinds of music.
"And human pleasures":
these are pools and bathhouses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section about שדים after the רב ששת story ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In קהלת 2:8, 'שרים ושרות' are kinds of music and 'תענוגות בני האדם' are pools and bathhouses.

steps.title: Two readings of 'שדה ושדות'
steps.stepSummary: In בבל they read 'שדה ושדות' as male and female demons, while in ארץ ישראל they read it as carriages.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'שדה ושדות': here in בבל they translated it as a male demon and female demons. In the West they said it means carriages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two different explanations of the last phrase of the פסוק. One comes from בבל and the other from ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שדה sounds like שד, a demon, so in בבל they took it to mean שלמה had male and female demons serving him. In ארץ ישראל they read it as שידתא, carriages, which fits the list of luxuries. The demon reading is the one the rest of the sugya builds on.

keyTerms.meaning: A male demon and female demons
In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: "Shidda and shiddot":
Here they translated it: a male demon and female demons.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means בבל, where this גמרא was learned.

phrases.english: In the West they said: carriages.
phrases.notes: 'The West' is ארץ ישראל, which lies west of בבל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes explaining the פסוק by interpreting its final phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'שדה ושדות' means male and female demons according to בבל, and carriages according to ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: 300 kinds of demons in שיחין
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says there were 300 kinds of demons in a place called שיחין, but he does not know what the 'שידה' itself is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: There were three hundred kinds of demons in שיחין, but I do not know what the שידה itself is.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a side fact about demons, which connects to the demon reading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He shows that there were many kinds of demons, 300 in one place alone. Even so, he admits he does not know the exact nature of the 'שידה' named in the פסוק. This honest uncertainty sits next to the בבל reading without cancelling it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת מִינֵי שֵׁדִים הָיוּ בְּשִׁיחִין,
phrases.english: There were three hundred kinds of demons in Shichin,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֵׁידָה עַצְמָהּ אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מָה הִיא.
phrases.english: but the shida itself, I do not know what it is.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת מִינֵי שֵׁדִים הָיוּ בְּשִׁיחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related statement about demons after the demon reading of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There were 300 kinds of demons in שיחין, but the exact nature of the 'שידה' is unknown.

steps.title: Why did שלמה need demons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the בבל reading and asks what שלמה needed male and female demons for.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: Here they translated it as a male demon and female demons. Male and female demons, what did he need them for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the earlier line about demons and asks a real question: what use did שלמה have for them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pools and music are obvious luxuries, but owning demons needs an explanation. The question sets up a long story that gives the reason. This is a question looking for information, not an attack on the reading.

keyTerms.meaning: For what did he need it?

phrases.english: The Master said: Here they translated it:
a male demon and female demons.
phrases.notes: This quotes back the בבל reading from step 12.

phrases.english: Male and female demons: what did he need them for?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the בבל reading in step 12 and asks for its purpose.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What purpose did male and female demons serve for שלמה?

steps.title: The בית המקדש had to be built without iron, so the חכמים point to the שמיר
steps.stepSummary: The answer begins: the פסוק says the בית המקדש was built without iron tools, so שלמה asked the חכמים how, and they told him about the שמיר that משה used.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And the house, when it was being built, was built of complete stone from the quarry, etc.' He said to the חכמים: How shall I do it? They said to him: There is the שמיר that משה brought for the stones of the אפוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering why שלמה needed demons. It first explains the problem that led to their use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says no iron tool was heard while the בית המקדש was being built, so the stones had to be cut some other way. The חכמים tell שלמה about the שמיר, which משה had used for the stones of the אפוד. That raises the next problem: where is the שמיר?

keyTerms.meaning: Complete stone ready from the quarry
The שמיר, a creature that could cut stone
The stones on the כהן גדול's אפוד

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And the house, when it was being built,
was built of complete stone from the quarry, etc."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 6:7. The rest of the פסוק says no iron tool was heard in the house.

phrases.english: He said to the Rabbis: How shall I do it?
They said to him: There is the shamir
that Moshe brought for the stones of the ephod.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וְהַבַּיִת בְּהִבָּנוֹתוֹ אֶבֶן שְׁלֵמָה מַסָּע נִבְנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 14 by setting up the need for the שמיר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שלמה needed a way to cut stones without iron for the בית המקדש, and the solution was the שמיר. The demons will be needed to find it.

steps.title: Where is the שמיר? Press the demons to find out
steps.stepSummary: שלמה asks where the שמיר is found, and the חכמים advise him to press a male and female demon together so they reveal it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Where is it found? They said to him: Bring a male demon and female demons and press them against each other. Perhaps they know and will reveal it to you.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward. Here we finally see why שלמה needed the demons: to get information about the שמיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step directly answers the question of step 14. The demons are a source of hidden knowledge, and the pressure is meant to make them tell what they know. The חכמים are not sure, though; they only say 'perhaps' the demons know.

keyTerms.meaning: Press them against each other, torment them together
And they will reveal it to you

steps.whyThisMatters: This line gives the real answer to 'why did שלמה need demons?' He used them to discover where the שמיר was.

phrases.english: He said to them: Where is it found?
They said to him: Bring a male demon and female demons
and press them against each other.
phrases.notes: He means: torment them together until they talk.

phrases.english: Perhaps they know and will reveal it to you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story and shows where the demons come in.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The demons were used to extract information about where the שמיר could be found.

steps.title: The demons do not know and point to אשמדאי
steps.stepSummary: שלמה presses the demons, but they say they do not know, and that perhaps אשמדאי, king of the demons, knows.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brought a male demon and female demons and pressed them together. They said: We do not know. Perhaps אשמדאי, king of the demons, knows.
steps.whatsHappening: שלמה follows the advice, but the demons cannot help. They send him on to אשמדאי, which sets up the next part of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plan only works partly: the demons give no location, but they do give a new lead. The search now moves to אשמדאי, king of the demons. This step leads into the next stage of the story rather than ending it.

phrases.english: He brought a male demon and female demons
and pressed them against each other.
They said: We do not know.
Perhaps Ashmedai, king of the demons, knows.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: אֲנַן לָא יָדְעִינַן, דִּילְמָא אַשְׁמְדַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the advice of step 16 and opens the next stage of the search.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The demons did not know where the שמיר was and pointed שלמה to אשמדאי, king of the demons.

steps.title: שלמה asks where אשמדאי is
steps.stepSummary: שלמה asks the demons where אשמדאי can be found.
steps.simpleTranslation: שלמה said to them: Where is he?
steps.whatsHappening: The demons just said that maybe אשמדאי knows where the שמיר is. Now שלמה asks where אשמדאי is, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The search moves one level up. The male and female demons did not know where the שמיר is, so שלמה now needs to find their king.

phrases.english: He said to them: Where is he?
phrases.notes: "He" means אשמדאי, the king of the demons from the step before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the demons' suggestion that אשמדאי knows.

steps.title: Where אשמדאי lives and his daily routine
steps.stepSummary: The demons describe אשמדאי's mountain, his sealed water pit, and his daily schedule.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told him: He is on a certain mountain. He dug a pit, filled it with water, covered it with a rock, and sealed it with his seal. Every day he goes up to heaven to learn in the heavenly yeshiva, then comes down to learn in the earthly yeshiva. Then he comes, checks his seal, opens the pit, drinks, covers it, seals it again, and leaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The demons answer שלמה. They tell him where אשמדאי is and describe his daily routine in detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The details matter for the plan that follows. אשמדאי only checks that his seal is whole, not what is inside the pit. That gives בניהו a way to trick him without breaking the seal.

phrases.english: They said to him: He is on such-and-such a mountain.
He dug himself a pit,
and filled it with water,
and it is covered with a rock,
and sealed with his seal;
and every day he goes up to heaven
and learns in the heavenly yeshiva,
and comes down to earth
and learns in the earthly yeshiva;
and he comes and checks his seal
and uncovers it and drinks,
and covers it, seals it, and goes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers שלמה's question from step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אשמדאי is on a certain mountain with a sealed water pit that he checks and drinks from every day.

steps.title: שלמה equips בניהו for the mission
steps.stepSummary: שלמה sends בניהו בן יהוידע with an engraved chain, an engraved ring, wool, and wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent בניהו בן יהוידע and gave him a chain with God's Name engraved on it, a ring with God's Name engraved on it, bundles of wool, and skins of wine.
steps.whatsHappening: שלמה picks בניהו for the job and gives him four tools. This step sets up the plan that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each tool has a role in the capture. The wool and wine are for tricking אשמדאי at the pit. The chain and ring carry God's Name, which gives them power over a demon.

keyTerms.meaning: A leading warrior in שלמה's court

phrases.english: He sent Benayahu son of Jehoiada,

phrases.aramaic: יְהַב לֵיהּ שׁוּשִׁילְתָּא דַּחֲקִיק עֲלַהּ שֵׁם,
phrases.english: and gave him a chain with the Name engraved on it,
and a ring with the Name engraved on it,
and bundles of wool, and skins of wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that שלמה knows where אשמדאי is, he sends someone to capture him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בניהו is sent with a holy chain and ring, wool, and wine.

steps.title: בניהו swaps the water for wine
steps.stepSummary: בניהו drains the pit's water from below, fills the pit with wine from above, plugs the holes, and hides in a tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and dug a pit lower down, drained the water out, and plugged the holes with the wool. Then he dug a pit higher up, poured in the wine, and closed them up. Then he climbed up and sat in a tree.
steps.whatsHappening: בניהו carries out the trick. He replaces the water in אשמדאי's pit with wine without ever touching the seal on top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the detail from step 19 that אשמדאי only checks his seal. Because the seal stays whole, אשמדאי will have no idea the pit was changed. The wool is used to plug the lower hole so the wine will not leak out.

phrases.english: He went and dug a pit from below,
and drained out the water,
and plugged them with the bundles of wool;
and he dug a pit from above,
and poured in the wine;
phrases.notes: Some versions have the round-bracket word, and the corrected wording is the one in square brackets. Either way it means "poured."

phrases.english: and he closed them up.
He climbed up and sat in a tree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: בניהו uses the tools from step 20 on the pit described in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pit's water is secretly replaced with wine while the seal stays whole.

steps.title: אשמדאי resists the wine, then drinks and sleeps
steps.stepSummary: אשמדאי finds wine in his pit, quotes two פסוקים against wine, refuses to drink, but finally drinks out of thirst, gets drunk, and falls asleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came, he checked the seal, opened the pit, and found wine. He said: It is written, "Wine is a mocker, strong drink is riotous; whoever strays by it will not be wise," and it is written, "Harlotry, wine, and new wine take away the heart." I will not drink. When he got thirsty he could not hold out. He drank, got drunk, and fell asleep.
steps.whatsHappening: אשמדאי falls into the trap. He knows wine is dangerous and even quotes פסוקים about it, but thirst wins and he ends up drunk and asleep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The demon who learns in the heavenly yeshiva knows exactly what the פסוקים warn. Still, he gives in once he is thirsty enough. His sleep is what gives בניהו the chance to act.

phrases.english: When he came, he checked the seal,
opened it, and found it full of wine.
He said: It is written: "Wine is a mocker, strong drink is riotous,
and whoever strays by it will not be wise,"
and it is written: "Harlotry, wine, and new wine take away the heart."
I will not drink.
When he got thirsty, he could not hold out;
he drank, got drunk, and fell asleep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the result of בניהו's trick from step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אשמדאי at first refuses the wine because of the פסוקים, but thirst wins and he falls asleep drunk.

steps.title: בניהו chains אשמדאי with God's Name
steps.stepSummary: בניהו comes down, puts the engraved chain on the sleeping אשמדאי, and when he struggles, warns him that his Master's Name is on him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came down, came over, threw the chain on him, and locked it. When he woke up, he started to struggle. He said to him: The name of your Master is on you! The name of your Master is on you!
steps.whatsHappening: בניהו captures אשמדאי while he sleeps. When the demon wakes up and tries to break free, בניהו tells him he cannot, because God's Name is on the chain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the engraved chain from step 20 is used. אשמדאי is strong enough to fight, but the holy Name stops him. He will not destroy something that carries his Master's Name.
steps.whatToRemember: אשמדאי is caught through a trick (the wine) and held through holiness (God's Name on the chain). Now שלמה can ask him about the שמיר.

phrases.english: He came down, came over, and threw the chain on him,
and locked it.
When he woke up, he was struggling;
He said to him: The name of your Master is on you!
The name of your Master is on you!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses אשמדאי's drunken sleep from step 22 to chain him with the chain from step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אשמדאי is bound by a chain bearing God's Name, which he will not break.

steps.title: אשמדאי knocks things down on the way, then reaches a widow's hut
steps.stepSummary: While בניהו leads the chained אשמדאי, אשמדאי knocks down a palm tree and a house. Then they reach a widow's small hut, and she comes out.
steps.simpleTranslation: When בניהו took אשמדאי and was coming back, they reached a palm tree. אשמדאי rubbed against it and knocked it down. They reached a house, and he knocked it down. They reached the small hut of a certain widow, and she came out.
steps.whatsHappening: The story keeps going. בניהו is bringing the chained אשמדאי back, and the גמרא sets up the next scene at the widow's hut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even in chains, אשמדאי is so strong that just brushing against a tree or a house knocks it over. The widow's hut is the next stop, and the line ends just as she comes out. What happens with her comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: He knocked it down, threw it over

phrases.english: When he took him and was coming,
he reached a palm tree – he rubbed against it and knocked it down;
phrases.notes: The one rubbing and knocking things down is אשמדאי.

phrases.english: he reached a house – he knocked it down;
he reached a small hut
belonging to a certain widow; she came out

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: None — this is a plain story line.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After בניהו chains אשמדאי in step 23, the story now follows the trip back and the damage אשמדאי causes on the way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: While being led in chains, אשמדאי knocks down a palm tree and a house, and then they reach a widow's hut, from which she comes out.
